name: Changchun Longjia International Airport
before:
The airport for both Changchun and Jilin City, 31 km north east of one and 76 km north west of the other, with the two cities sharing responsibility for running it. It is a regional hub for China Southern.

The rail connection is unusually neat. Longjia railway station sits in the basement of the terminal, on the Changchun to Jilin intercity line, so a passenger can walk from arrivals onto a train. Coaches also run into both cities, and a metro line is planned.

The airport opened in August 2005, replacing the joint civil and military field at Dafangshen, and was expanded between 2009 and 2011 with two more international gates and a bigger apron. That work made it possible to take wide bodies as large as a 747.

International routes reach Bangkok, Seoul, Singapore, Tokyo, Osaka and Hong Kong, and Air China opened a direct link to Frankfurt in 2021, which makes this one of the main international gateways for north east China.
after:
The airport for both Changchun and Jilin City, 31 km north east of Changchun and run by Jilin's provincial airport group, part of Capital Airport Holding. China Southern has a base here.

The rail connection is unusually neat. Longjia railway station, on the Changchun to Jilin intercity line, is underground at the airport, so a passenger can walk from arrivals onto a train. Airport buses also run into Changchun, and a metro line is planned.

It opened in August 2005, replacing the joint civil and military field at Dafangshen. Expansion in phases since 2009 has added a second terminal.

The airport counts eight international and regional destinations, among them Bangkok, Hong Kong and Vladivostok.

claims.inAfter: Longjia railway station, on the Changchun to Jilin intercity line, is underground at the airport, so a passenger can walk from arrivals onto a train
claims.note: Was 'sits in the basement of the terminal'. The operator places the underground station just south of Terminal 1, reached on foot through an underground passage, with an underground corridor to Terminal 2; Wikipedia puts it at the basement of the terminal. Both agree it is underground and walkable, so the text says that. The operator calls the line China's first intercity railway with zero transfer to an airport, which bears out 'unusually neat'. Trains take 14 minutes to Changchun station and 30 to Jilin (operator; not added).
